chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Mi'za, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who rents out land and then sub-rents it for more than he rented it for, he said: 'There is no harm, for this is not like the shop or the laborer; for the profit of the laborer and the shop is forbidden.'

key_terms.الْمُزَارَعَة: Sharecropping or leasing land for cultivation

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to rent land and then sub-rent it for a higher price in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits sub-leasing agricultural land at a higher rate, distinguishing it from the prohibition on sub-leasing a shop (*hanut*) or a laborer (*ajir*). This ruling highlights the unique nature of land as a productive asset where value addition is permissible, unlike the direct sale of utility in shops or labor. The distinction underscores the Shia juristic principle that the prohibition applies to the commodification of specific utilities rather than all forms of lease transfers.
